prerequisites: Windows German keyboard layout and physical Right Alt/AltGr.

Enable left Ctrl/left Alt swap and test AltGr+0 in the same editor.

reproduce.expected_result: AltGr+0 continues to insert the expected brace because the configuration does not remap right Alt.

proposed_fixes.title: Investigate AltGr with left modifier remaps
proposed_fixes.root_cause: AltGr may be represented as Right Alt plus synthesized Ctrl, and Keyboard Manager's left-Ctrl remap may alter that synthesized state.
plan: Reproduce AltGr+0 with only the reported left modifier mappings and capture events before/after remapping.
Trace distinction between Right Alt/AltGr, left Ctrl, and layout-synthesized Ctrl.
If conflation is confirmed, preserve AltGr while applying explicit left-side remaps and add layout-aware tests.
verification: On German layout, confirm AltGr+0 inserts braces in two apps before and after remapping.
Run focused tests for left/right Ctrl/Alt and AltGr-generated input.

issue_context.summary: On a German keyboard, swapping left Ctrl and left Alt reportedly breaks AltGr curly braces despite no right-Alt mapping; the author later supplied a configuration screenshot.
known_information: Report identifies German layout, left Ctrl/left Alt swap, and AltGr+0 no longer inserting braces across Edge and Notepad++.
Latest author comment (2023-11-23) says only left-key mappings were active and attaches a configuration screenshot.
inferences: The remapper may conflate AltGr's synthesized Ctrl with explicitly remapped left Ctrl or disturb right-Alt state; neither path is confirmed.
issue_context.analysis: Cross-application reproduction and clarified configuration narrow the investigation to AltGr/right-Alt behavior. Reproduce and inspect event classification before proposing a specific correction.
